findings.description: `ts.getLeadingCommentRanges(text, pos)` skips any comment that sits before the first CR/LF after `pos`, except at `pos === 0`. TypeScript counts those as trailing comments of the previous token. U+2028 doesn't switch collection on either. The walk only asks for leading ranges at each token's full start, so it never sees a pragma that follows code on the same line. Typical cases are `cond ? /* v8 ignore next */ x() : y()`, `a(); /* v8 ignore start */` and `x = /* @__PURE__ */ f()`. The printer drops it too. The raw scanner at fa84a8c saw every comment trivia, so this is a new gap.
findings.body:
**Same-line pragmas are invisible to `pragmaAnchors`, so a push that adds one is skipped as comment-only**

```ts
for (const range of ts.getLeadingCommentRanges(text, node.pos) ?? []) {
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/07fa0d537d2712706a9f4ea654dbadd08559a7f9/tools/review/src/preflight.utils.ts#L102-L115

`getLeadingCommentRanges(text, pos)` reports nothing until it crosses the first CR/LF after `pos`, except at `pos === 0`. TypeScript treats comments before that line break as trailing comments of the previous token. So a pragma that follows code on the same line is never tested against `PRAGMA`:

- `const a = cond ? x() : y();` -> `const a = cond ? /* v8 ignore next */ x() : y();`
- `const x = f();` -> `const x = /* @__PURE__ */ f();`
- `log(x);` -> `log(x); // eslint-disable-line no-console`
- `run();` -> `run(); /* c8 ignore start */`

The printer runs with `removeComments: true`, and both sides yield `[]` anchors. So `sameCodeIgnoringComments` returns true and `decideMode` returns `skip-comment-only`. The scanner at fa84a8c anchored every comment token, so the regression is new in 07fa0d5. It also breaks the README's promise to "keep every pragma ... before the same code".

There's a sign in the code too: when `pos` isn't 0, `hasLineBreak` (L111) is always `true`. The test at L204 (`risky(); /* v8 ignore next */` moved to its own line) passes only because the before side has no anchor at all.

**Fix:** also collect the same-line ranges with `getTrailingCommentRanges` at the same position, and skip them at `pos === 0`, where leading ranges already start collecting. The two calls split the trivia at its first CR/LF. Together they cover every comment exactly once, and `hasLineBreak` then tells the two kinds apart again. Add tests where only the after side has a same-line pragma, e.g. `same("a();\nb();\n", "a(); // @ts-ignore\nb();\n")` and the ternary case above. Both should be `false`.
findings.suggestion:
const trailing = node.pos === 0 ? [] : (ts.getTrailingCommentRanges(text, node.pos) ?? []);
    for (const range of [...trailing, ...(ts.getLeadingCommentRanges(text, node.pos) ?? [])]) {

findings.description: The PR description's Markdown bullet still says the prose allowlist includes "design chapters 00 to 08". Commit 07fa0d5 removed them from `isProseMarkdown`, so at head only root README/CONTRIBUTING/CHANGELOG qualify and every `docs/` file is always reviewed.
The preflight row has a stray space before a period: "`ci/review-metrics` . Rebases".

The `isProseMarkdown` JSDoc says "Everything else steers an agent". That overclaims: the same commit's tests list `tools/x/notes.md`, which steers nothing. The real rule is that only root repo meta is known to be inert, so "Everything else may steer an agent" would be accurate.

`read` in `sameCodeIgnoringComments` is named like a plain parse, but it parses, returns `null` on diagnostics, and serialises a `[printed, anchors]` pair into a JSON equality fingerprint. A name like `fingerprint` would make that contract visible.

`pragmaAnchors` still encodes each anchor as a `${tokenIndex}:${hasLineBreak}:${comment}` string. The shape stays implicit, and the `:` separator is unambiguous only because `comment` comes last. Since the result is only stringified and compared, a tuple array would show the shape without the encoding.
